blocks.text: Lots and land in Thornhill
Streets, schools and getting around Thornhill

items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge, BC. The City describes Thornhill as a heavily forested, mainly residential area with several farms and nurseries, with a large mountain-biking and hiking trail network on 256 Street (17 trails, typically about an hour each). SnapStats lists "Thornhill" as a sub-area under Maple Ridge.
Main roads and commute: Dewdney Trunk Road and Lougheed Highway along the south side; 248, 256 and 264 Streets north–south; 100 Avenue and 112 Avenue east–west on the hillside.

Transit: route 748 (Thornhill / Haney Place) is a loop from Haney Place via 240 Street, McClure Drive, Jackson Road, 100 Avenue, 256 Street, 98 Avenue, 264 Street and 268 Street, weekday and Saturday trips only at wide intervals; route 701 runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road along the south side. No West Coast Express station in this sub-area.

Schools (Ministry-listed names/addresses only): Whonnock Elementary, 27471 112 Avenue; Albion Elementary, 10031 240 Street; Blue Mountain Elementary, 12453 248 Street; Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary, 10445 245 Street; Garibaldi Secondary, 24789 Dewdney Trunk Road. SD42 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12).

Recreation and services: the 256 Street trail network (City description in the first bullet); Kanaka Creek Regional Park at the west side; Whonnock Lake Park in Whonnock to the east. No recreation centre or library branch inside this sub-area — Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and Maple Ridge Public Library, 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in the Town Centre. Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street (24/7 emergency); Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 121 – 11900 Haney Place, 7 days, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

blocks.text: Good to know about Thornhill

items.t: The 249 Street parcels are labelled Thornhill but describe themselves as Albion.

The bus that serves the hillside runs at wide intervals, weekdays and Saturdays only. Route 748's Thornhill loop is not a frequent-service corridor — acreage buyers here are driving; price the lot on today's service, not on any corridor plan (the adopted Lougheed corridor ends at 221 Street, west of here).

Parcel sizes / zones —: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 minimum lot areas: A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha, RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha depending on the zone text.

Serviced vs unserviced ground: rural properties here may be on wells and septic — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Thornhill

items.t: Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019: — minimum lot areas A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha, RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha per the zone text; verify a specific parcel's exact zone with the City before pricing any use.

Suites and SSMUH: one secondary suite per lot in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area; on ALR parcels the ALR Use Regulation governs instead (suite inside the principal residence only, s.31; additional residence only under s.32). Eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws — on rural/ALR ground the ALC frame above controls first.

If a strata purchase is made here (the three townhome complexes): Pad ground is not lot stock / land / acreage; pad tenancy percentages only (2026 = 2.3% + proportionate; 2027 = 2.2% + proportionate), no pad-rent dollar figure as fact.

Thornhill: streets and boundaries

items.t: Thornhill is a heavily forested, mainly residential area in east Maple Ridge with several farms and nurseries.
Thornhill sits east of the Albion planning area, in School District 42's (SD42) East Capital Zone, which Kanaka Creek bisects with limited bridge crossings.
Its working corridor is Dewdney Trunk Road and 256 Street, with 100 Avenue and 98 Avenue through the housing on the Thornhill bus loop.

blocks.text: Thornhill: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is rural-residential: detached houses on large parcels, farms and nurseries, not urban subdivisions.

Farm-edge lots fall under the RS-3 (Agricultural) and A1–A3 zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019; the City's RS-3 checklist requires a lot over 0.4 hectares for an agricultural use, tied to Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) land or an agricultural Official Community Plan (OCP) designation.

blocks.text: Thornhill: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Urban development is not supported yet: OCP policy 3-24 keeps Thornhill a long-term Urban Reserve until city population exceeds 100,000 and capacity inside the existing urban area approaches build-out.

Policy 3-25 first requires a Metro Vancouver-approved Regional Context Statement amendment, a Fraser Sewerage Area extension, and an adopted Area Plan including an aquifer groundwater study and an agricultural impact assessment.

blocks.text: Thornhill: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Thornhill's bus, the 748 Thornhill/Haney Place loop, is a limited community-shuttle service, not a frequent route.
The City counts a mountain biking and hiking network on 256 Street: 17 trails, moderately difficult, typically about an hour each.
Kanaka Creek Regional Park's Canyon Trail links the Bell-Irving fish hatchery to Cliff Falls, 1.2 kilometres one way; the hatchery supports chum and coho salmon enhancement.
Rural lots can depend on wells; the Province's well records service is searchable for a property's well.

blocks.text: Thornhill: development and new projects

items.t: North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan, both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue: approximately 500 acres. Status: OCP amending bylaw adopted June 23, 2026; the plan approves no construction, and future proposals need separate applications and environmental reviews (as of November 3, 2026).
Funded 256 Street and Dewdney Trunk Road intersection improvements: status design in 2026, construction anticipated 2027 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Thornhill: getting around

items.t: Route 748 loops from Haney Place via 240 Street, Jackson Road and 100 Avenue, then 256 Street, 98 Avenue, 264 Street and 268 Street, some trips via Port Haney Station.
There is no West Coast Express station in Thornhill; Port Haney, reached on some 748 trips, is the rail connection.

blocks.text: Thornhill: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check slope and creek setbacks lot by lot: City agricultural checklists flag geotechnical reports, fish and wildlife review and a DP30 area check here.
Check ALR status on the ALC map, and the well record for any lot not on community water; neither map shows parcel-level flood or slide risk.
